findings.text: 经常重开同一项开发任务的 DSH 开发者，可以让代理在新会话找回此前交接的测试入口和工作约定。
Cordis 挂载代理生命周期、提示、会话日志与工具。读取经过 Honcho SDK，首步追加消息，后续通过宿主运行时上下文传递。
本次为 package 0.1.4 定版源码，覆盖配置、SDK 调用接口、捕获和注入，未复现服务策略或真实宿主结果。
包清单公开发布并以 prepare 构建为 lib；核对的是固定仓库版本和写入路径，未验证 npm tarball 与固定源码相同。

#### 启动与依赖

| 依赖或条件 | 是否必需 | 用途 | 缺失或不满足时 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| DSH 的 tools 和 systemPrompt | 必需 | 接入模型工具与提示 | 插件需要这些服务；确切版本组合尚未验收 |
| Honcho 凭据及端点 | 必需 | 会话检索与外部持久化 | 无密钥停用；仅凭据库条目不被解析 |
| sessionQuery | 捕获必需 | 提供持久会话事件 | 无服务则不能持续上传自动捕获 |
| commands | 诊断可选 | 提供人工状态和刷盘命令 | 没有 /honcho，需要日志和服务侧核对 |

#### 成本

| 阶段 | 现金与资源成本 | 人工与时间投入 | 已知条件与未知项 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 首次 | 需要可访问的 Honcho 服务或部署资源，费用未知 | 核对 profile、凭据和工作区边界 | 默认配置可立即准备捕获 |
| 持续 | 检索、推断、上传及模型提示的额外资源 | 核对错误、来源和长期记忆内容 | 自动捕获默认启用，时延与账单未测 |
| 失败恢复与退出 | 重发、后端保留与清理成本未知 | 回查会话和发送范围，停止插件并切回项目说明 | 停用不是服务端数据删除 |
先用只含模拟信息的测试工程验证一次交接。准备两组同名测试项目和一个独立工作区，检查每个新会话的来源。如果还不能确认哪些内容离开本机，停用组件并用本地项目说明接续工作。[Q02](#research-q02) [Q04](#research-q04)

#### 效果

| 效果项 | 当前证据支持 | 尚不能确定 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 首次以往资料召回 | 启动有等待预算和追加记忆的代码 | 资料准确率、会话作用域和首轮耗时 |
| 会话捕获与重试 | 存在选择、批次与成功后推进游标的机制 | 半批失败重试的服务端去重与完整性 |
| 读写可观察性 | /honcho 可显示同步时点、错误与提示抑制 | 具体 DSH 配置及多项目并行下的可用性 |
首步避免直接信任提示注册的时序，后续异步刷新降低对网络等待的依赖。同会话上传串行并推进持久游标，游标写失败和部分批已确认仍需服务侧配合验证。
把以前需人工粘贴的项目交接放进 DSH 的请求路径，先用有上限的首步等待获取资料，后续保持后台刷新，并给出可观察读取状态的诊断入口。主要机制依赖 Honcho 服务和 DSH 宿主挂载。[Q01](#research-q01) [Q03](#research-q03)
开箱即有自动对话上传，正则脱敏只覆盖已知格式。关闭对话捕获后仍可能发送检索查询或主动保存的文本，同名目录和共享工作区也可能扩大记忆范围。[Q01](#research-q01) [Q02](#research-q02)
可按项目保存带出处的经人确认的决策卡，只渲染本任务相关项，用跨项目标记与错误率检验能否兼得回忆和数据范围。这项设计尚待验证。[Q04](#research-q04)

technical.rationale: Honcho 的记忆能力和共享配置源于上游，本接入的局部创新是把首轮追加消息、后续异步提示与可观测状态放在一起。它实际改动首步与后续等待取舍，可借鉴到具有可修改首步决策和提示上下文的宿主。发送侧增量游标减少自行维护队列的工作，服务去重和跨会话隔离仍有待核查。[Q01](#research-q01) [Q02](#research-q02) [Q03](#research-q03)

business.rationale: 对反复重开会话的团队，手工交接可以部分转为自动出现在提示中的历史资料，工作流有实质变化。交付物仍是同种编码任务，单一团队项目中的优势有限。已有 Honcho 工作区的 DSH 用户获得一条接入路径，未测的服务费和维护时间无法证明结构性回报。[Q01](#research-q01) [Q04](#research-q04)

recommendation.reason: 反复重开编码会话的 DSH 开发者可以在隔离的 Honcho 工作区用模拟资料找回上一轮约定的测试入口。相比每次手动复制交接笔记，插件能在模型首次请求前尝试取得历史资料，节省的时间仍需实测。用户发现跨项目资料或无法核对出站内容时，应停用插件并回到本地项目说明。

scenario.rationale: [Q01](#research-q01) 的 pre-step 注入对应每次重开项目时重复交代入口的摩擦，[Q04](#research-q04) 把合格结果具体为能否正确选测试入口和说清来源，超过仅列场景。没有实际需求频率和现有说明不足的材料，未达充分档。

advantage.rationale: [Q01](#research-q01) 的首步消息和 runtime 刷新能主动召回超过存档入口的历史，超出局部便利。配对实验和可靠性尚不明，且来源过滤及同名目录可降低可审计性，尚不能判为实质改善。

evidence.rationale: [Q01](#research-q01) 的包与首步入模，[Q02](#research-q02) 的捕获游标与失败，[Q03](#research-q03) 的诊断支持源码级低敏试用，覆盖面高于只确认接线。固定组合未运行，无法升执行证据档。

cost.rationale: [Q02](#research-q02) 的同步错误和 [Q03](#research-q03) 的命令可排查，[Q04](#research-q04) 给出隔离和退回项目说明的方法，高于退出重要环节不明的档。凭据、外部服务和上传后处置需人工，持续时间和账单未实测，未达负担较轻档。

publication.summaries.text: 通过 Honcho 为 DeepSeek Harness 提供跨会话持久记忆、历史检索和信息保存。

items.模型工具: honcho_search 检索历史和结论，honcho_chat 请求记忆推断，honcho_remember 保存信息。
items.用户命令: /honcho 检查连接、捕获和注入状态，config 查看解析结果，flush 手动刷盘。
items.事件监听: 监听代理首步与会话事件以读取记忆、注入提示并增量捕获对话。

publication.capabilities.table:
| 能力 | 主要用途 | 使用条件与边界 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 提示记忆 | 让模型看到用户画像、会话摘要及相关结论 | 与首步／后续装配时序和外部响应有关 |
| 会话上传 | 把选取的对话文字写入 Honcho | 依赖 sessionQuery，可关闭，正则脱敏具有漏检边界 |
| honcho_search | 查询消息和派生结论 | 依赖工作区范围、有结果才返回 |
| honcho_chat | 询问偏好或历史决策的推断 | 外部请求，结果适宜核对 |
| honcho_remember | 主动持久化结论 | 直接提交文本，避免输入敏感内容 |
| /honcho | 查看捕获、读取和作用域相关状态 | 宿主注入 commands 后方可使用 |

      "path": "README.md",
      "content": "# dsh-honcho\n\n[![Listed on dsh-plugin.org](https://dsh-plugin.org/badges/listed.svg)](https://dsh-plugin.org/plugins/plastic-labs/dsh-honcho)\n\nEnglish | [中文](README.zh.md) | [Русский](README.ru.md)\n\nPersistent memory for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness), powered by\n[Honcho](https://honcho.dev).\n\n`dsh` forgets everything when a session ends. This plugin gives it memory that doesn't: what you're building,\nhow you like to work, what you decided last week and why. It reads the same `~/.honcho/config.json` as the\nother Honcho integrations, so there is one place to configure all of them — and pointing two of them at the\nsame `workspace` gives them one shared memory.\n\n## Install\n\n```sh\ndsh plugin --profile <name> add @honcho-ai/dsh-honcho\n```\n\nThen put your API key and name in `~/.honcho/config.json`:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"peerName\": \"your-name\",\n  \"auth\": { \"apiKey\": \"${HONCHO_API_KEY}\" },\n  \"hosts\": {\n    \"dsh\": { \"workspace\": \"dsh\" }\n  }\n}\n```\n\nGet a key at [app.honcho.dev](https://app.honcho.dev). `HONCHO_API_KEY` in the environment also works on its\nown — the config file is only needed to change defaults.\n\n## What it does\n\n**Injects what Honcho knows at the start of a session** — your peer card, a summary of this project's session so\nfar, and the conclusions Honcho has drawn that are relevant to what you just asked. One API call, shaped to a\ncharacter budget, refreshed as you work.\n\n**Captures every turn.** User and assistant messages go to Honcho in the background, debounced, and flushed at\nturn boundaries, before compaction, and on shutdown. Common secret formats are redacted first (API keys and\ntokens, `password:`/`secret:` fields, private keys, JWTs, cookies, connection strings, credential URLs). This is\nregex matching, so it is best-effort: an unusual format, or a bare high-entropy string with no label, can still\nget through. Add your own with `capture.noisePatterns`, or turn capture off with `capture.saveMessages`.\n\n**Gives the model three tools:**\n\n| Tool              | For                                                                        |\n| ----------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\n| `honcho_search`   | Looking something up. Searches raw messages _and_ derived conclusions.     |\n| `honcho_chat`     | Asking a question of judgment. Reasons over everything Honcho knows. Slow. |\n| `honcho_remember` | Saving a durable fact, preference, or decision.                            |\n\n**`/honcho`** shows status and a link to the session in the Honcho dashboard — see Commands below.\n\n## Configuration\n\nEverything behavioral lives in `~/.honcho/config.json` under `hosts.dsh` — the same file `claude-honcho`,\n`codex-honcho`, and the other integrations read. Root holds identity and connection; the host block holds\nbehavior.\n\nThe file is read as strict JSON: the comments and trailing commas below are annotation only. Leave them in and\nthe whole file is skipped without a warning, so every setting falls back to its default.\n\n```jsonc\n{\n  \"peerName\": \"your-name\",\n  \"workspace\": \"honcho\",\n  \"baseUrl\": \"https://api.honcho.dev\", // bare host or …/v3 both fine\n  \"timeoutMs\": 30000,\n  \"auth\": { \"apiKey\": \"${HONCHO_API_KEY}\" },\n  \"enabled\": true, // global kill switch\n  // sessions may also sit here as a fallback; the host block wins\n\n  \"hosts\": {\n    \"dsh\": {\n      \"workspace\": \"dsh\",\n      \"aiPeer\": \"dsh\", // defaults to the host name\n      \"observationMode\": \"unified\", // unified | directional\n      \"sessionStrategy\": \"per-directory\", // see Sessions below\n      \"sessionPeerPrefix\": true, // session names are <peer>-<dir>\n      \"sessionPrefix\": \"\", // literal prefix on every generated name, e.g. \"vps-\"\n      \"sessions\": { \"/path/to/repo\": \"pinned-session-name\" }, // pin a session\n      \"injection\": {\n        \"sessionStart\": [\"directives\", \"summary\", \"peerCard\"], // + representation\n        \"perTurn\": [\"userContext\", \"dialectic\"], // userContext = representation + card\n        \"tools\": true,\n        \"searchTopK\": 10,\n        \"searchMaxDistance\": 0.6,\n        \"maxConclusions\": 15, // how many conclusions Honcho RETURNS\n        \"maxRenderedConclusions\": 4, // how many survive filtering into the prompt\n        \"contextTokens\": 1500,\n        \"cadence\": { \"dialectic\": 5, \"ttlSeconds\": 300 },\n        \"dialectic\": {\n          \"reasoning\": \"low\", // minimal | low | medium | high | max\n          \"maxChars\": 600,\n        },\n      },\n      \"capture\": {\n        \"saveMessages\": true,\n        \"saveToolUse\": false, // one-line summaries of tool activity\n        \"writeFrequency\": \"async\", // async | sync\n        \"noisePatterns\": [], // additive to the built-in secret patterns\n      },\n      \"messageUpload\": {\n        \"maxUserTokens\": 6000,\n        \"maxAssistantTokens\": 6000,\n      },\n    },\n  },\n}\n```\n\n### Injection components\n\nThe two menus differ in **cadence**, not in what they can carry.\n\n`injection.sessionStart` is injected once when a session opens: `directives` (guidance on using memory),\n`summary`, `peerCard`, `representation`.\n\n`injection.perTurn` refreshes as you work:\n\n- **`userContext`** — a fresh, prompt-scoped peer context blob: **representation + peer card**, retrieved using\n  your current message as the search query so recall is associative rather than merely recent. It is a bundle,\n  so it supplies both regardless of what `sessionStart` names. To get one without the other, name it in\n  `sessionStart` and set `perTurn: []` — at the cost of per-turn refresh.\n- **`dialectic`** — a reasoned answer about you, run every `cadence.dialectic` turns and shaped by\n  `injection.dialectic`. Nothing waits on it after the first turn, so a late answer reaches the next one.\n\nComponents the canonical schema names but this plugin does not implement — `briefing`, `assistantContext`,\n`sessionContext` — are reported at startup rather than silently dropped, as are schema keys it does not act on\n(`showContents`, `statusline`, `globalOverride`, granular `observation`, `multiUser`) and any key renamed since\nan earlier version. Nothing here is accepted and quietly ignored.\n\nThe plugin's own `cordis.yml` config carries plumbing only — `configPath`, `apiKeyRef`, `host`, `enabled`. Set\n`host` to run a credential-isolated profile (`\"dsh_work\"`) against the same install.\n\n### Sharing memory with other integrations\n\nEach integration defaults to its own Honcho `workspace` — `dsh` here, `claude_code` for claude-honcho — and a\nworkspace is the isolation boundary, so **by default they do not see each other's memory.** Point them at the\nsame `workspace` to merge them:\n\n```jsonc\n\"hosts\": {\n  \"dsh\":         { \"workspace\": \"shared\" },\n  \"claude_code\": { \"workspace\": \"shared\" }\n}\n```\n\nKeep `peerName` identical across them too, since conclusions are stored per peer. `sessionStrategy:\n\"git-remote\"` and `sessionPrefix` are proposed for claude-honcho as well, so a repo worked on from both can be\npointed at one session on purpose rather than by accident.\n\n### Sessions\n\nDefault: one long-lived session per project directory, named `<peerName>-<dir>`, matching claude-honcho. Pin a\ndifferent name for any path with the root `sessions` map — an override always wins.\n\n| `sessionStrategy`         | Session name            | Notes                                                              |\n| ------------------------- | ----------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |\n| `per-directory` (default) | `<peer>-<dir>`          | Stable across restarts and branches                                |\n| `per-repo`                | `<peer>-<repo-root>`    | Same memory from any subdirectory                                  |\n| `git-remote`              | `<peer>-<host-owner-repo>` | From the `origin` URL, so the same repo on two machines is one session. Falls back to `per-directory` outside a repo or without an `origin` |\n| `git-branch`              | `<peer>-<dir>-<branch>` | Falls back to `per-directory` outside a repo or on a detached HEAD |\n| `per-session`             | `<peer>-chat-<id>`      | A clean slate every restart                                        |\n| `global`                  | `<peer>`                | One memory for everything                                          |\n\n`per-directory` and `per-repo` name a session after a folder, so two different projects that both live in a\n`web` directory silently share one memory across machines. `git-remote` is the fix: it reduces the `origin` URL\nto `host/owner/repo`, so `git@github.com:you/web.git` and `https://github.com/you/web` agree, and `you/web` and\n`someone-else/web` do not. It compares the URL as configured, so machines that clone through different ssh\n`Host` aliases — `github.com-work` on one, `github.com` on the other — still get separate sessions.\n\n**`sessionPrefix`** puts a literal string in front of every generated name — `\"vps-\"` gives `vps-you-web` — for\nwhen the machine a session came from should be visible in it. It applies to every strategy. A name pinned in\n`sessions` is used exactly as written and is never prefixed.\n\n**Prefer the wider scopes.** Honcho's guidance is not to scope sessions too thin: the background Deriver needs\na single session to accumulate enough material before it can reason well. `git-branch` splits a project's\nmemory per branch, and `per-session` discards it on every restart.\n\n## Commands\n\n| Command          | Does                                                                               |\n| ---------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\n| `/honcho`        | Status: peer, workspace, session, strategy, pending uploads, last sync, last fetch |\n| `/honcho config` | Resolved settings, the file they came from, and any ignored injection components   |\n| `/honcho flush`  | Sync now                                                                           |\n\n## Requirements\n\n- Node `^22.19.0 || >=24.0.0`\n- A running `dsh`, `0.1.2-rc.1` or later (typechecked against `0.2.1-rc.2`; tested on `0.1.2-rc.1` through `0.2.1-rc.4`)\n- A Honcho API key, or a self-hosted Honcho at `baseUrl`\n\n## Development\n\n```sh\nbun install\nbun test\nbun run typecheck\nbun run build\n```\n\nSee [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md) for the design and the reasoning behind each extension point.\n\n## Credit\n\n[**dsh-honcho-sync**](https://github.com/nanpaidashi/dsh-honcho-sync) by\n[@nanpaidashi](https://github.com/nanpaidashi) (MIT) inspired the initial design of this plugin\n\nThe `~/.honcho/config.json` contract, the session-naming convention, and `src/redact.ts` come from the sibling\nHoncho integrations — [claude-honcho](https://github.com/plastic-labs/claude-honcho),\n[codex-honcho](https://github.com/plastic-labs/codex-honcho), and their relatives.\n\n[DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) is MIT-licensed, and its\n[Cordis](https://github.com/cordiverse/cordis) plugin model is what made a native integration worth writing\ninstead of a hook bridge.\n\n## License\n\nMIT\n"

      "content": "/**\n * Best-effort secret redaction for anything uploaded to Honcho.\n *\n * Started as a port of claude-honcho (`plugins/honcho/src/redact.ts`) and has\n * since grown the formats that port missed (see the second half of\n * DEFAULT_RULES). Regex-based, so novel secret formats still pass through, and\n * some common ones cannot be matched at all without redacting ordinary text (a\n * bare 40-character AWS secret looks like any hash). Users extend the defaults\n * via `capture.noisePatterns`.\n *\n * This runs on EVERY captured message, not only tool summaries. A coding\n * harness has whatever is on screen in its buffer — pasted keys, .env contents,\n * customer data — and capture without scrubbing is an exfiltration path.\n */\n\ninterface RedactRule {\n  pattern: RegExp;\n  replacement: string;\n}\n\n/** Names that mark a value as secret. `tokens` (as in `max_tokens`) and `pwd` (the shell's\n *  working directory) are deliberately left out of the colon-style rules below. The affixes\n *  are bounded because unbounded `[\\w-]*` on both sides backtracks quadratically (tens of seconds on a long word). */\nconst SECRET_NAME = String.raw`[\\w-]{0,64}(?:password|passwd|secret|token(?!s)|api[_-]?key|access[_-]?key|credentials?)[\\w-]{0,64}`;\n\n/** A double-quoted string body, honoring backslash escapes so `\"a\\\"b\"` is one value. */\nconst DQ = String.raw`\"(?:[^\"\\\\]|\\\\.)*\"`;\n\nconst DEFAULT_RULES: RedactRule[] = [\n  // KEY=value assignments with a secret-bearing key (PGPASSWORD=..., AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=...)\n  {\n    pattern:\n      /\\b(\\w*(?:PASSWORD|PASSWD|PWD|SECRET|TOKEN|API_?KEY|ACCESS_KEY|CREDENTIALS?)\\w*)\\s*=\\s*(\"[^\"]*\"|'[^']*'|[^\\s;|&\"']+)/gi,\n    replacement: \"$1=***\",\n  },\n  // --password / --token style CLI flags\n  {\n    pattern: /(--(?:password|passwd|pwd|token|api-?key|secret|auth)[= ])(?:\"[^\"]*\"|'[^']*'|[^\\s;|&\"']+)/gi,\n    replacement: \"$1***\",\n  },\n  // Authorization headers\n  {\n    pattern: /(authorization:\\s*(?:bearer|basic|token)\\s+)[^\\s\"']+/gi,\n    replacement: \"$1***\",\n  },\n  // Credentials embedded in URLs (scheme://user:pass@host)\n  {\n    pattern: /([a-z][a-z0-9+.-]*:\\/\\/[^/\\s:@]+:)[^@\\s]+@/gi,\n    replacement: \"$1***@\",\n  },\n  // Well-known token shapes: Honcho, AWS, OpenAI/Anthropic-style sk-, GitHub, Slack, GitLab, npm\n  {\n    pattern:\n      /\\b(?:hch[_-]?[A-Za-z0-9_-]{16,}|AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}|sk-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{16,}|(?:ghp|gho|ghu|ghs|ghr)_[A-Za-z0-9]{20,}|github_pat_[A-Za-z0-9_]{20,}|xox[baprs]-[A-Za-z0-9-]{10,}|glpat-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,}|npm_[A-Za-z0-9]{36})\\b/g,\n    replacement: \"***\",\n  },\n  // ── Formats the first five rules miss ──────────────────────────────────────\n  // Private key blocks\n  {\n    pattern: /-----BEGIN [A-Z ]*PRIVATE KEY-----[\\s\\S]*?-----END [A-Z ]*PRIVATE KEY-----/g,\n    replacement: \"***\",\n  },\n  // JWTs\n  {\n    pattern: /\\beyJ[A-Za-z0-9_-]{8,}\\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]{8,}\\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]{4,}/g,\n    replacement: \"***\",\n  },\n  // JSON fields with a secret-bearing name: \"api_key\": \"…\"\n  {\n    pattern: new RegExp(String.raw`(\"${SECRET_NAME}\"\\s*:\\s*)(?:${DQ}|[^\\s,}\\]]+)`, \"gi\"),\n    replacement: '$1\"***\"',\n  },\n  // YAML / header style: password: …, api-key: …, X-Api-Key: …\n  {\n    pattern: new RegExp(String.raw`\\b(${SECRET_NAME}\\s*:\\s*)(?!\\*\\*\\*)(?:\"[^\"]*\"|'[^']*'|[^\\s,;]+)`, \"gi\"),\n    replacement: \"$1***\",\n  },\n  // Cookie headers carry session ids under arbitrary names\n  { pattern: /\\b((?:set-)?cookie\\s*:\\s*)[^\\r\\n]+/gi, replacement: \"$1***\" },\n  // Prose: \"密码是 …\"\n  { pattern: /((?:密码|口令)\\s*(?:是|为|[:：])\\s*)\\S+/g, replacement: \"$1***\" },\n  // Azure connection strings and SAS keys\n  { pattern: /\\b((?:AccountKey|SharedAccessKey|SharedAccessSignature)=)[^;\\s\"']+/gi, replacement: \"$1***\" },\n  // Slack incoming-webhook URLs\n  { pattern: /https:\\/\\/hooks\\.slack\\.com\\/services\\/[A-Za-z0-9/_-]+/g, replacement: \"***\" },\n  // More token shapes: Stripe secret/restricted keys, Google API keys, Telegram bot tokens\n  {\n    pattern: /\\b(?:(?:sk|rk)_(?:live|test)_[A-Za-z0-9]{16,}|AIza[0-9A-Za-z_-]{35}|\\d{8,10}:[A-Za-z0-9_-]{30,})/g,\n    replacement: \"***\",\n  },\n];\n\n/** Validate a user-supplied pattern. Returns an error message, or null if it compiles. */\nexport function validateRedactPattern(source: string): string | null {\n  try {\n    new RegExp(source);\n    return null;\n  } catch (e) {\n    return `Invalid regex ${JSON.stringify(source)}: ${e instanceof Error ? e.message : String(e)}`;\n  }\n}\n\n/**\n * Redact secrets from `text`. `extraPatterns` are additive to the built-in\n * defaults. Patterns that fail to compile are skipped rather than throwing —\n * a hand-edited config file must not be able to break capture.\n */\nexport function redactSecrets(text: string, extraPatterns?: readonly string[]): string {\n  let result = text;\n  for (const rule of DEFAULT_RULES) {\n    result = result.replace(rule.pattern, rule.replacement);\n  }\n  for (const source of extraPatterns ?? []) {\n    try {\n      result = result.replace(new RegExp(source, \"gi\"), \"***\");\n    } catch {\n      continue;\n    }\n  }\n  return result;\n}\n"

      "path": "src/tools.ts",
      "content": "/**\n * Model-facing Honcho tools.\n *\n * Three, deliberately. claude-honcho registers eleven and the community\n * dsh plugin shipped twenty-five before cutting to four for context efficiency\n * — every schema costs tokens on every request.\n *\n * These go through `defineTool`, NOT a raw `ToolDefinition`. The two accept\n * different shapes: `defineTool` takes a per-property DSL that it compiles into\n * an implicit object root, while `ctx.tools.register()` on its own expects\n * finished JSON Schema. Handing the DSL straight to `register()` produces a\n * schema with no `properties`, so the model can call the tool but cannot pass\n * it anything — every call arrives with empty arguments.\n */\n\nimport { defineTool, type ToolDefinition, type ToolRunContext } from \"@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools\";\nimport type { ResolvedConfig } from \"./core-shim.js\";\nimport { describeError } from \"./errors.js\";\nimport { escapeFence } from \"./memory.js\";\n\n/** Honcho SDK surface we depend on, narrowed to what these tools call. */\nexport interface HonchoGateway {\n  /** Reasoned dialectic answer about a peer. Slow — 2–5 minutes is normal. */\n  chat(query: string, options: { targetPeerId?: string; sessionId?: string }): Promise<string>;\n  /** Full-text/semantic search over messages. */\n  searchMessages(query: string, limit: number): Promise<string[]>;\n  /** Semantic search over derived conclusions — the reasoned layer. */\n  searchConclusions(query: string, limit: number): Promise<string[]>;\n  /** Persist a durable fact about the user. */\n  remember(content: string, sessionName: string): Promise<void>;\n  currentSessionName(cwd?: string, dshSessionId?: string): string;\n}\n\n/**\n * Canonical output for all three: one text field the renderer surfaces.\n * A fresh object per tool so each `defineTool` call infers its own arg type;\n * `additionalProperties` is required on an object value schema.\n */\nfunction textOutput() {\n  return {\n    schema: {\n      type: \"object\",\n      // Required-ness is per-property here; the value schema DSL rejects a\n      // top-level `required` array (typecheck accepts it, the runtime does not).\n      properties: { text: { type: \"string\", required: true } },\n      additionalProperties: false,\n    },\n    // dsh requires an ARRAY of content blocks here; a bare string fails at\n    // runtime with \"content is not iterable\".\n    render: (_args: unknown, value: { text: string }) => [{ type: \"text\" as const, text: value.text }],\n  } as const;\n}\n\nfunction sessionOf(exec: ToolRunContext): [cwd: string | undefined, id: string | undefined] {\n  const session = (exec.agent as { session?: { id?: string; header?: { cwd?: string } } } | undefined)?.session;\n  return [session?.header?.cwd, session?.id];\n}\n\nexport function createTools(config: ResolvedConfig, honcho: HonchoGateway): ToolDefinition[] {\n  return [\n    defineTool({\n      name: \"honcho_search\",\n      description:\n        \"Search the user's Honcho memory across all past sessions. Returns both raw messages and derived \" +\n        \"conclusions. Use when you need history beyond what was already injected into context.\",\n      parameters: {\n        query: {\n          type: \"string\",\n          required: true,\n          description: \"The search query to find relevant information from past sessions.\",\n        },\n        limit: { type: \"number\", description: \"Results per source (default 5, max 10).\" },\n      },\n      output: textOutput(),\n      async execute(args) {\n        const query = args.query.trim();\n        if (!query) return { text: \"Search query was empty.\" };\n        const limit = Math.min(Math.max(args.limit ?? 5, 1), 10);\n        // Both layers, in parallel. Messages alone miss everything the Deriver\n        // and Dreamer inferred; conclusions alone miss what was actually said.\n        const [messages, conclusions] = await Promise.all([\n          honcho.searchMessages(query, limit).catch((e: unknown) => [`[message search failed: ${describeError(e)}]`]),\n          honcho.searchConclusions(query, limit).catch((e: unknown) => [`[conclusion search failed: ${describeError(e)}]`]),\n        ]);\n        const lines = [...messages, ...conclusions].map(escapeFence);\n        return { text: lines.length ? lines.join(\"\\n\") : \"No results in messages or conclusions.\" };\n      },\n    }),\n\n    defineTool({\n      name: \"honcho_chat\",\n      description:\n        \"Ask Honcho a reasoned question about the user, answered over everything it has learned across all \" +\n        \"sessions. Use for questions of judgment or preference — how they like to work, what they would \" +\n        \"prefer — rather than for looking up something that was said.\",\n      parameters: {\n        query: {\n          type: \"string\",\n          required: true,\n          description: \"The question to ask about the user based on their history.\",\n        },\n      },\n      output: textOutput(),\n      async execute(args, exec) {\n        const query = args.query.trim();\n        if (!query) return { text: \"Question was empty.\" };\n        const sessionName = honcho.currentSessionName(...sessionOf(exec));\n        // observationMode decides who is asking about whom: unified queries the\n        // user peer directly; directional asks from the AI peer's perspective.\n        const targetPeerId = config.observationMode === \"directional\" ? config.peerName : undefined;\n        try {\n          const answer = await honcho.chat(query, { targetPeerId, sessionId: sessionName });\n          return { text: escapeFence(answer.trim()) || \"Honcho has nothing relevant on that yet.\" };\n        } catch (e) {\n          return { text: `Honcho could not answer: ${describeError(e)}` };\n        }\n      },\n    }),\n\n    defineTool({\n      name: \"honcho_remember\",\n      description:\n        \"Save a durable fact, preference, or decision about the user to Honcho so it survives into future \" +\n        \"sessions. Use when the user states something worth carrying forward, not for transient task detail.\",\n      parameters: {\n        content: {\n          type: \"string\",\n          required: true,\n          description: \"The information to remember about the user for future sessions.\",\n        },\n      },\n      output: textOutput(),\n      async execute(args, exec) {\n        const content = args.content.trim();\n        if (!content) return { text: \"Nothing to remember — `content` was empty.\" };\n        try {\n          await honcho.remember(content, honcho.currentSessionName(...sessionOf(exec)));\n          return { text: \"Saved to Honcho memory.\" };\n        } catch (e) {\n          return { text: `Could not save to Honcho: ${describeError(e)}` };\n        }\n      },\n    }),\n  ];\n}\n"

      "path": "src/commands.ts",
      "content": "/**\n * `/honcho` — human commands, executed against the agent without creating a\n * model message.\n *\n * `last successful sync` is not decoration. Injection is fire-and-forget and a\n * failed fetch reuses the previous snapshot, so a Honcho outage otherwise looks\n * exactly like a working plugin. This is where that becomes visible.\n */\n\nimport type { CommandResult } from \"@deepseek-ai/dsh-commands/types\";\n\nimport { sessionUrl, unsupportedComponents, type ResolvedConfig } from \"./core-shim.js\";\nimport { describeError } from \"./errors.js\";\nimport { hostHeaderValue, pluginHeaderValue, type TelemetryIdentity } from \"./telemetry.js\";\nimport type { Capture } from \"./capture.js\";\n\n// dsh's registry rejects results without a `kind` discriminator.\nconst ok = (text: string): CommandResult => ({ kind: \"success\", text });\nconst fail = (text: string): CommandResult => ({ kind: \"error\", text });\n\nexport interface CommandDeps {\n  /** A getter, not a value: capture is wired inside a `ctx.inject` on the\n   *  `sessionQuery` seam, so it can appear or disappear after this command is\n   *  registered. */\n  capture(): Capture | undefined;\n  sessionNameFor(cwd: string | undefined): string;\n  cwdOf(agent: unknown): string | undefined;\n  /** Timestamp of the last successful memory fetch, or undefined. */\n  lastFetchAt(): number | undefined;\n  /** Message from the last failed memory fetch, if the latest attempt failed. */\n  lastFetchError(): string | undefined;\n  injectionActive(): boolean;\n  /** True when a deployment or agent preset is suppressing runtime context. */\n  injectionSuppressed(): boolean;\n  /** Path the shared config file was read from. */\n  configFile(): string;\n  /** The identity every Honcho request is carrying right now. */\n  telemetry(): TelemetryIdentity;\n}\n\n/** Capture can be configured on but not yet wired, so report the difference\n *  rather than showing \"on\" for something that is uploading nothing. */\nfunction captureStatus(config: ResolvedConfig, capture: Capture | undefined): string {\n  if (!config.capture.saveMessages) return \"off (capture.saveMessages)\";\n  if (!capture) return \"unavailable — ctx.sessionQuery is not mounted\";\n  const tools = config.capture.saveToolUse ? \" +tools\" : \"\";\n  return `on${tools} · ${capture.pending()} pending · last sync ${ago(capture.lastFlushedAt())}`;\n}\n\nfunction ago(at: number | undefined): string {\n  if (!at) return \"never\";\n  const seconds = Math.round((Date.now() - at) / 1000);\n  if (seconds < 60) return `${seconds}s ago`;\n  if (seconds < 3600) return `${Math.round(seconds / 60)}m ago`;\n  return `${Math.round(seconds / 3600)}h ago`;\n}\n\n/** The three telemetry header values, as one line; `?` for what is not known. */\nfunction clientIdentity(identity: TelemetryIdentity): string {\n  const parts = [hostHeaderValue(identity) ?? \"?\", pluginHeaderValue(identity) ?? \"?\"];\n  if (identity.model) parts.push(identity.model);\n  return parts.join(\" · \");\n}\n\nexport interface CommandDefinition {\n  name: string;\n  description: string;\n  input: { hint: string };\n  handler(invocation: { agent: unknown; rawInput?: string }): Promise<CommandResult>;\n}\n\nexport function createCommand(config: ResolvedConfig, deps: CommandDeps): CommandDefinition {\n  return {\n    name: \"honcho\",\n    description: \"Honcho memory status. `config` shows resolved settings, `flush` syncs now.\",\n    input: { hint: \"config | flush\" },\n    async handler({ agent, rawInput }) {\n      const sub = (rawInput ?? \"\").trim().toLowerCase();\n      const cwd = deps.cwdOf(agent);\n      const name = deps.sessionNameFor(cwd);\n\n      if (sub === \"flush\") {\n        const capture = deps.capture();\n        if (!capture) return ok(\"Capture is off — nothing to flush.\");\n        try {\n          await capture.flushAll();\n          return ok(`Flushed to Honcho session \\`${name}\\`.`);\n        } catch (e) {\n          return fail(`Flush failed: ${describeError(e)}`);\n        }\n      }\n\n      if (sub === \"config\") {\n        // Resolved values, not per-key provenance: tracking the source layer for\n        // every key roughly doubles the resolver, and the file path plus the\n        // resolution order in the docs answers the same question.\n        const redacted = { ...config, apiKey: config.apiKey ? `${config.apiKey.slice(0, 7)}…` : \"(unset)\" };\n        const ignored = unsupportedComponents(config.injection);\n        const lines = [\n          `config file  ${deps.configFile()}`,\n          \"\",\n          JSON.stringify(redacted, null, 2),\n        ];\n        if (ignored.length) {\n          lines.push(\"\", \"ignored injection components:\");\n          for (const [name, reason] of ignored) lines.push(`  ${name} — ${reason}`);\n        }\n        return ok(lines.join(\"\\n\"));\n      }\n\n      if (sub && sub !== \"status\") {\n        return fail(`Unknown subcommand \\`${sub}\\`. Use \\`/honcho\\`, \\`/honcho config\\`, or \\`/honcho flush\\`.`);\n      }\n\n      const fetchError = deps.lastFetchError();\n      const lines = [\n        `peer         ${config.peerName}`,\n        `ai peer      ${config.aiPeer}`,\n        `workspace    ${config.workspace}`,\n        `session      ${name}`,\n        `endpoint     ${config.baseUrl}`,\n        `observation  ${config.observationMode}`,\n        `strategy     ${config.sessionStrategy}`,\n        `capture      ${captureStatus(config, deps.capture())}`,\n        `injection    ${deps.injectionActive() ? \"active\" : \"inactive\"} · last fetch ${ago(deps.lastFetchAt())}`,\n        `client       ${clientIdentity(deps.telemetry())}`,\n      ];\n      if (deps.injectionSuppressed()) {\n        lines.push(\"⚠ runtime context is suppressed by this composition — injected memory is not reaching the model\");\n      }\n      if (fetchError) lines.push(`⚠ last fetch failed: ${fetchError}`);\n      const uploadError = deps.capture()?.lastError();\n      if (uploadError) lines.push(`⚠ last upload failed: ${uploadError}`);\n      if (!config.apiKey) lines.push(\"⚠ no API key — set HONCHO_API_KEY or auth.apiKey in ~/.honcho/config.json\");\n      lines.push(\"\", sessionUrl(config.workspace, name));\n      return ok(lines.join(\"\\n\"));\n    },\n  };\n}\n"
